security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown formatting, ordinary imports, serialization constants, or readable Chinese documentation rather than threats. Backup creation can overwrite an earlier backup within one second. Additional risks include malformed variable patches, partial patch commits, and symbolic-link writes; no malicious intent or exfiltration evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Second-resolution backup names allow consecutive writes to overwrite the same backup.
remediation.suggestion: Create backups with exclusive, collision-resistant filenames and retain each original backup rather than replacing an existing file.

remediation.issue: Variable plans replace complete Marshal integer nodes with payload bytes that omit the integer type marker.
remediation.suggestion: Require integer nodes, prepend the Marshal integer marker, and test generated patches by reparsing complete saves before writing.

remediation.issue: Patch application writes successful patches even when other patches fail validation.
remediation.suggestion: Reject the entire plan when any patch fails; perform all validation before backing up or modifying files.

remediation.issue: The predictable temporary filename can follow an existing symbolic link and truncate another file.
remediation.suggestion: Use exclusive temporary-file creation in the target directory, reject symbolic links, and clean up safely before atomic replacement.

semantic_findings.title: Variable Patches Omit the Marshal Integer Type Marker
semantic_findings.description: The variable planner replaces an entire serialized node with encode_int output, which encodes only its payload. The missing integer marker can corrupt saves.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reader consumes a type byte before read_int, while the planner replaces the full node with encode_int payload alone. This directly contradicts the format.

semantic_findings.title: Failed Patch Validation Does Not Prevent Partial Writes
semantic_findings.description: Invalid patches are skipped, but valid patches are still committed and the apply command returns success. Interdependent changes can leave inconsistent save state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The failed list is printed, but only an empty applied list prevents writing. Mixed valid and invalid patches therefore produce partial saves.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Temporary Files Permit Symbolic-Link Clobbering
semantic_findings.description: atomic_write writes through a predictable .allcg-tmp path without exclusive creation. A preexisting symbolic link can redirect truncation to another writable file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.write_bytes follows an existing symbolic link before os.replace runs. Exploitation requires control of the temporary directory entry and writable destination permissions.

content.user_title: Prepare Gallery Unlock Patches for Offline Game Saves
content.value_statement: Gallery progress can be difficult to locate inside local game saves. This skill inspects saves and prepares reviewable patches with default backups and rollback.
actual_capabilities: Search common local save locations and rank candidates by filename, extension, modification time, and game-directory relevance.
Identify several game engines from installation-directory signatures.
Parse Ruby Marshal streams and inspect compatible RGSS switch and variable arrays.
Compare save snapshots at byte level and infer candidate unlock layouts from single-byte changes.
Generate patch plans for selected RGSS switches and variables, although variable encoding currently has an identified integrity defect.
Preview and apply patches, create default backups, verify expected bytes, and restore recorded backups.
limitations: Only user-owned offline single-player games are in scope; multiplayer, anti-cheat, and online validation are excluded.
Dedicated engine tooling focuses on compatible RGSS saves; other engines require manual format analysis or useful snapshot differences.
Encrypted, compressed, signed, or custom saves may require separate tooling, and gallery field meanings are not automatically established.
Variable encoding, partial patch commits, and temporary-file handling have integrity defects; rapid writes can also overwrite backups.

use_cases.title: Find a Local Gallery Save
use_cases.description: Locate candidate saves for an owned offline game and inspect likely engine information before choosing a target.

use_cases.title: Compare Controlled Unlock Snapshots
use_cases.description: Compare snapshots before and after one gallery unlock to identify candidate state bytes without distributing game assets.

use_cases.title: Review RGSS Gallery Switch Changes
use_cases.description: Inspect compatible test saves and prepare targeted switch plans for confirmed gallery IDs before manual validation.

prompt_templates.title: Locate Candidate Saves
prompt_templates.prompt: Find candidate saves for my owned offline game [game name] in [installation directory]. Report likely paths and engine clues without modifying files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: locate saves without writing patches.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an RGSS Save
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my RGSS save at [absolute save path]. Summarize streams, switches, and variables. Do not assume which IDs control galleries or change files.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Unlock Snapshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [absolute snapshot A], [absolute snapshot B], and [absolute snapshot C] after separate gallery unlocks. Explain candidate offsets and stride uncertainty without applying changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: evaluate evidence from controlled snapshots.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Targeted Switch Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a dry-run switch plan for [absolute save path] using confirmed gallery IDs [IDs]. Use absolute paths and preserve an independent original backup. Report failed patches, integrity risks, and rollback steps. Do not apply changes until I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a narrowly scoped plan before approval.

output_examples.input: Locate saves for my offline game without changing files.
output: Candidate report: likely saves are ranked by path relevance, extension, and modification time.
Engine assessment: installation signatures suggest RPG Maker VX Ace.
Status: no save changes were made; confirm the intended save before further analysis.

output_examples.input: Review a switch plan before applying it.
output: Scope: only the gallery switch IDs you confirmed are included.
Preflight: review the target hash, original bytes, planned offsets, and any failed patches.
Decision: leave the save unchanged until approval and preserve an independent backup.

best_practices: Close the game and preserve an independent original backup before generating or applying any plan.
Use absolute input paths, inspect every dry run, and reject plans with failed patches or uncertain gallery fields.
Prefer confirmed switch IDs, avoid variable patches until encoding is fixed, and validate results inside the game.
anti_patterns: Enable every switch without confirming which IDs control gallery state.
Apply external or stale plans without reviewing their target, hashes, offsets, and expected bytes.
Use the skill on multiplayer or protected online saves, or rely on one rapidly overwritten backup.

faq.question: Does this skill work with every game engine?
faq.answer: No. Dedicated tooling targets compatible RGSS saves. Other engines require manual analysis or informative byte differences.

faq.question: Can it identify every gallery switch automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can inspect switches and infer candidate byte layouts, but game-specific gallery meanings require confirmation.

faq.question: Can I use it for online or multiplayer games?
faq.answer: No. The documented scope excludes multiplayer, online validation, anti-cheat systems, and competitive games.

faq.question: Are backups and rollback available?
faq.answer: Yes, by default. Keep an independent backup because second-resolution names can collide and rollback depends on recorded backup metadata.

faq.question: Are variable patches safe to apply?
faq.answer: The current variable planner omits a Marshal type marker and can corrupt saves. Avoid applying variable plans until this defect is fixed.

faq.question: What happens when some patches fail validation?
faq.answer: The current patcher can still write the remaining patches. Reject mixed-result plans and resolve every failure before applying changes.
